explain: A small protocol adapter delegates to an existing authorized domain function. Business rules stay at the service boundary so other entry points cannot bypass them.
steps: Validate the authenticated principal against document ownership. || Return a bounded excerpt through the adapter.
name: read-tool-service

explain: The MCP Python SDK v1 FastMCP interface registers a typed function as a tool and runs a stdio server. Use a compatible v1 release for this example; v2 has a different documented server interface.
steps: Install a compatible optional mcp v1 SDK (mcp>=1,<2) in an isolated environment. || Register a bounded read-only synthetic tool and start it using the SDK's stdio entry point.
expect: A client sees the synthetic_excerpt tool; a valid call returns Exchange only.
limit: Optional SDK integration sketch: syntax-checked only; not executed by offline checks. The synthetic tool has no real user identity or private data.
name: mcp-sdk-registration

explain: Contract tests exercise rejection and output limits as well as a happy path. All assertions use a local synthetic function without remote capabilities.
steps: Define the tool's accepted identity and maximum result size. || Assert valid behavior and expected validation failures.
name: tool-contract-tests

explain: A semaphore bounds simultaneous work inside one process. This does not establish a fleet-wide quota or a durable command identity.
steps: Acquire the semaphore before entering the simulated tool. || Count maximum active calls and ensure it never exceeds the bound.
name: tool-concurrency

explain: Tool telemetry records safe operation metadata and distinguishes execution errors from business outcomes. Payloads and secrets are omitted.
steps: Construct one event after a successful transport returning not_found. || Preserve the business outcome instead of turning it into a transport exception.
name: tool-observation
